lead.headline: THREE BENGALURU COMPANY EMPLOYEES DIE AFTER WAVES SWEEP GROUP INTO SEA
lead.deck: The workers were part of a 16-member team on an outing near Gokarna; two others were rescued
paragraphs: Three employees of a Bengaluru-based company died after powerful waves swept five members of their group into the sea at Dubbanshashi Beach near Gokarna on Sunday. Two people were rescued by lifeguards and local fishermen.
The 16-member team had travelled from Bengaluru for an outing. Police said the bodies of all three employees had been recovered and that an investigation was under way.
Authorities advise visitors to heed local beach safety directions and warnings about sea conditions.

sidebarStory.headline: STATE BUS FARES SET TO RISE FROM NOVEMBER 5
sidebarStory.subhead: BMTC’s fare-review panel recommended a 40% increase; the final rates are due after Wednesday’s meeting
paragraphs: The Karnataka government says revised fares for its four state-run transport corporations will take effect on November 5. Transport officials are to finalise the fare structure at a meeting on November 4; the committee’s recommendation is not the final price.

stories.headline: CCTV LEADS TO ARREST IN VAO EXAM MALPRACTICE CASE
stories.deck: Police allege the Haveri district topper used Google Lens to scan questions during the test
paragraphs: Police said CCTV footage showed Shankar Bannur using a mobile phone during the October 4 Village Administrative Officer recruitment exam. Investigators allege he scanned questions with Google Lens; the 31-year-old, who scored 151 out of 200, has been arrested.

stories.headline: KSRTC TO ADD 2,600 SPECIAL BUSES FROM BENGALURU FOR DEEPAVALI
paragraphs: The state road transport corporation plans extra services from Bengaluru between November 6 and 8, with return services on November 10 and 11. Departures will use Kempegowda Bus Station, Mysuru Road and Shantinagar, among other terminals.

stories.headline: BENGALURU SKILL SUMMIT OPENS A THREE-DAY WORKFORCE MEET
paragraphs: The second Bengaluru Skill Summit runs November 3–5 at The Lalit Ashok. Its programme centres on workforce development, future-ready skills and collaboration between industry, government and training institutions.

stories.headline: ₹53,866-CRORE DEAL SIGNED FOR EIGHT NEXT-GENERATION CORVETTES
stories.deck: Indian shipyards GRSE and Goa Shipyard will build five and three vessels respectively
paragraphs: The Defence Ministry signed contracts worth ₹53,866.50 crore for eight Next Generation Corvettes for the Indian Navy. Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers will build five; Goa Shipyard will build three.
The ministry says the vessels will be designed by the Navy and built by the two public-sector shipyards, with advanced weapons and sensor systems.

stories.headline: FIRE AT HPCL’S VISAKHAPATNAM REFINERY BROUGHT UNDER CONTROL
paragraphs: A fire broke out at the refinery on Monday night, police said. Six fire tenders responded and the blaze was brought under control within an hour; no casualties were reported. The cause remains unknown.

stories.headline: OCTOBER GST COLLECTIONS REACH ₹2.31 LAKH CRORE
paragraphs: Gross GST revenue rose 22.9% year on year to ₹2,31,290 crore in October, according to government data. The tally was the second-highest monthly collection on a comparable basis since the tax was introduced in 2017.

stories.headline: TEEN ASSAULT VICTIM STABLE AFTER 11-HOUR SURGERY IN BENGALURU
stories.deck: The 14-year-old remains critically ill and on ventilator support at Manipal Hospital
paragraphs: Doctors at Manipal Hospital said the girl, transferred from Andhra Pradesh after an alleged chainsaw attack at her school, was stable after nearly 11 hours of surgery. She remains critically ill in intensive care and may need further procedures.

stories.headline: ED ATTACHES ₹427 CRORE IN ALLEGED BELAGAVI PONZI CASE
paragraphs: The Enforcement Directorate says it has provisionally attached assets linked to an alleged ₹2,459-crore scheme in Belagavi. The agency says more than 35,000 investors were involved; the investigation is ongoing.

stories.headline: DEVAHALLI-BORN SCIENTIST TO LEAD NASA INTERSTELLAR-DUST MISSION
paragraphs: Astronomer Ramya Manjunath Anche, raised in Devanahalli, will lead NASA’s $20-million PUFFINS mission. Its small telescope is being designed to study interstellar dust and is expected to launch in 2030.

stories.headline: LAKSHYA SEN WINS SEVENTH CAREER TITLE AT HYLO OPEN
stories.deck: The Indian defeated Jonatan Christie in straight games in Sunday’s final
paragraphs: Lakshya Sen beat Indonesia’s Jonatan Christie 21–17, 21–10 to win the Hylo Open men’s singles title on Sunday, ending a season-long wait for a tour victory.

stories.headline: POLICE SET 8–10 PM WINDOW FOR DEEPAVALI FIRECRACKERS
paragraphs: Karnataka Police say crackers should be used only from 8 pm to 10 pm during Deepavali. Their guidance calls for green crackers and advises against fireworks in public places and crowded areas.
